portable_rule: C++ TCK sources may include only the official RTI API headers and the C++ standard library. Shared ordinary-service scenario IDs are reused from the Java TCK catalog. Provider selection, link inputs, compile definitions, transport endpoints, and fault-injection fixtures belong to an adapter profile.
promotion_rule: A promoted scenario has passed the portable source-boundary check and every callback model declared for its adapter lane. Unless a scenario declares a narrower callback_models list with a non-empty callback_model_scope_note, this means both HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE. Candidate scenarios remain opt-in until that evidence is recorded; availability status separately describes required adapter capabilities.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: Clause 4 assigns this rule to joined federates: they shall interact with the RTI in accordance with the HLA interface specification. The RTI provider's obligations are the service signatures and semantics in the detailed API requirements, which have their own public C++ TCK cases. A standalone positive test that merely invokes RTIambassador would add no distinct observable behavior and would misleadingly inflate direct coverage.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: This is not direct C++ TCK coverage and does not establish that arbitrary federate applications follow the binding. It does not waive any RTI C++ API/service obligation or its detailed tests; it scopes out only a separate Summary Rule 4 test because the summary adds no independent RTI behavior beyond those service contracts.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: Clause 4 assigns each federate the obligation to have an OMT-documented SOM. The public RTI API accepts and composes supplied FOM modules, but it cannot determine whether those documents are the application's complete SOM or whether they describe the application's internal simulation model. Mapping a successful model lookup or Join to this application-level artifact obligation would overstate the evidence.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: This is not direct C++ TCK coverage and does not claim that any arbitrary federate application has a complete, OMT-conformant SOM. It does not waive RTI-side OMT parsing, schema validation, federation-model composition, or Join Federation Execution obligations; the existing additional-FOM TCK scenario covers one bounded module-composition path only.

requirement_dispositions.owner_role: federate application using the RTI time-management service family
requirement_dispositions.rationale: Clause 4 assigns the high-level ability to manage local time for coordinated data exchange to federates. The portable C++ TCK already has distinct service-level witnesses, including cpp-tck.time-advance-contract for selected time-role/grant/query behavior and cpp-tck.timestamped-interaction-tar-equal-boundary plus cpp-tck.timestamped-interaction-tar-inclusive-target-delivery for TSO delivery before a TAR grant. Mapping those same observations again to the umbrella statement would not add a distinct normative assertion; the federate application's time policy and orchestration remain outside RTI control.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: This is not direct Clause 4 C++ TCK coverage and does not establish that arbitrary federate applications coordinate local time correctly. It does not waive, validate, or aggregate any RTI time-management service obligation; each API and delivery requirement retains its own exact C++ TCK mapping and scope. This disposition does not claim full Clause 8 coverage, a complete time-advance-service matrix, interoperability, or conformance.

requirement_dispositions.owner_role: federate application using the RTI time-management service family
requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516-2025 §6.5 Rule 10 repeats the federate-level requirement to manage local time for coordinated exchange. The selected C++ TCK cases exercise individual RTI time-advance and TSO ordering contracts; treating their existing service assertions as a separate §6.5 test would add no independent observable criterion for the federate's overall time-management policy.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct §6.5 C++ TCK mapping or coverage is claimed. This disposition does not waive any RTI time-management API requirement, nor claim that all such services are tested or that arbitrary federate time policies are correct. Existing service-specific mappings remain bounded to their cited clauses and assertions.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516-2025 §5.4 places the obligation on joined federates to use the HLA Interface Specification. The portable C++ TCK is RTI-side evidence: its federate code intentionally issues standard API calls to observe provider behavior. A positive interaction or other service case therefore does not establish that arbitrary federate applications use the interface correctly, and mapping generic API use to §5.4 would duplicate the exact per-service RTI requirements without a distinct observable criterion.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct §5.4 C++ TCK mapping or coverage is claimed. This disposition does not waive any IEEE 1516.1-2025 C++ binding signature or service-semantic requirement, each of which retains its own mapping and test scope; it does not establish interface-wide conformance or correctness of arbitrary joined federate applications.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: Clause 5.2 allocates simulation-associated object-instance representation to federates rather than the RTI. This is an internal architecture invariant: the official C++ API exposes service outcomes, not RTI data-storage boundaries. A TCK can verify values sent by federates are communicated, but cannot prove which process or component retains internal representation. Avoid treating message flow as direct evidence; verify this requirement through RTI architecture/source review.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct Clause 5.2 C++ TCK mapping or test pass is claimed. This does not mark the architecture requirement satisfied: provider architecture/source review remains outstanding. The disposition only explains why the public-API TCK cannot establish it.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: Clause 6.1 assigns each federate the obligation to have an HLA SOM documented in accordance with the HLA OMT. The RTI API accepts and composes supplied FOM modules but cannot determine whether a supplied document is the application’s complete SOM or whether it describes the application’s internal simulation model. A successful FOM creation or lookup case therefore cannot prove this application-level artifact obligation.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct Clause 6.1 C++ TCK mapping or coverage is claimed. This does not establish that arbitrary federates have complete, OMT-conformant SOMs and does not waive RTI-side FOM parsing, schema validation, model composition, or Join Federation Execution obligations.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: Clause 6.1 governs whether object models and tools are assessed for conformance and when a product may publicly use the HLA Conforming label. A portable RTI C++ TCK cannot certify products, publish certified results, or authorize that label.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct C++ TCK mapping, certification result, or label authorization is claimed. This disposition does not represent Umbra as certified and does not waive individual RTI API requirements.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.2-2025 §7 p. 101 l. 38 is a framing sentence introducing the following FOM/SOM combination rules. It defines no distinct table row, FOM element, RTI service result, or state transition apart from those child rules. Portable C++ TCK cases map directly to individual child outcomes; mapping one public Create case to this umbrella sentence would overstate its scope.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.2-2025 §4.1.2 p. 35 l. 64 specifies the Model Identification table's categories, required information, and NA placeholders as object-model documentation. The Requirements Lab classifies this record as cross-cutting document content, not modeled RTI state. The RTI-consumed IEEE1516-DIF-2025 XSD makes modelIdentification optional and all its data fields optional, and the official C++ RTI API has no operation to retrieve or assess arbitrary Model Identification tables.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct C++ TCK mapping or pass is claimed for completeness of the Model Identification table or its NA placeholders. This author-responsibility disposition does not waive RTI obligations to parse supplied FOM content and does not claim validation, interoperability, or conformance.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.2-2025 §4.1.3 p. 38 l. 71 requires the Model Identification categories across FOMs, FOM modules, SOMs, and SOM modules. The Requirements Lab classifies this as cross-cutting document content. The public C++ RTI API neither accepts SOM documents as RTI services nor enumerates the Model Identification categories across arbitrary model documents; the DIF schema also permits omission of modelIdentification.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct C++ TCK mapping or pass is claimed for completeness of Model Identification data across all FOM/SOM artifacts. The disposition does not waive RTI processing obligations for supplied modules or claim validation, interoperability, or conformance.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.2-2025 §4 p. 50 l. 14 specifies D/A capability annotations in a SOM or SOM module and the corresponding federate publication premise. The official IEEE 1516.1-2025 C++ RTI API accepts FOM module paths for federation creation but exposes no SOM input or query operation. A portable C++ RTI TCK cannot inspect an arbitrary federate's SOM declaration; FOM-based ownership-transfer cases remain separate runtime evidence for their mapped 1516.1 service requirements.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct C++ TCK mapping or pass is claimed for the SOM D/A table annotation or completeness of that model-authoring responsibility. This disposition does not waive 1516.1 runtime requirements for publication, acquisition, or divestiture; those behaviors require their own direct service mappings. It is not validation, interoperability, or conformance evidence.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.2-2025 §4 p. 55 l. 53 assigns each federate its local dimension value type and semantics and explicitly requires the federate to provide the normalization function mapping its view to the RTI view. The official IEEE 1516.1-2025 C++ API exposes RTI dimension upper bounds and get/set region range bounds, but no operation to supply or execute an application-specific dimension normalization function. A portable RTI TCK cannot decide whether arbitrary domain-specific coordinate conversions are correct.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct C++ TCK mapping or pass is claimed for application-owned dimension semantics, value types, or normalization policy. This disposition does not waive the RTI's separate obligations to process supplied RTI-space ranges and apply DDM filtering, which require their own direct runtime evidence; it is not application-normalization validation, cross-federate interoperability, or conformance evidence.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.2-2025 §4 p. 56 l. 27 assigns the Dimension table's Output Data Semantics cell to describe human-authored federation-view semantics and says to enter NA when that information is unnecessary. The official C++ RTI API exposes dimension handles, names, upper bounds, and region ranges, but no operation to retrieve or judge the adequacy of this prose or whether NA is semantically appropriate. The existing public-Create rejection of an empty cell checks table validity only; it cannot validate the prose's meaning.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct C++ TCK mapping or pass is claimed for the correctness or necessity of Output Data Semantics prose. Existing dimension-table field tests cover selected empty-cell rejection and acceptance of populated rows, not semantic adequacy. This ownership disposition is not a waiver of valid-FOM parsing requirements, and it is not implementation validation or conformance evidence.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.12.1 p. 378 l. 42 requires a federate to switch from one RTI C++ implementation to another without recompiling or relinking. The public C++ API has no operation that exercises provider replacement, and the current installed-package adapter supplies only the Umbra provider. A direct oracle requires a second independently conforming provider under the same ABI contract; a one-provider run cannot establish replacement compatibility.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct C++ TCK mapping or pass is claimed for cross-provider replacement. This is not implementation validation, conformance evidence, or a waiver of the RTI interoperability obligation. Revisit with an independent provider in the TCK provider matrix.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §6.8 requires handle equality between joined federates using different language APIs. A portable C++-only TCK scenario can create and compare C++ handles but cannot create or observe a handle through the Java API; same-language C++ equality is not a witness for this cross-language requirement. The current installed-package C++ adapter declares no mixed-language participant fixture, and the separate Java JNI TCK lane does not by itself establish that both bindings joined the same federation.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct C++ TCK mapping or pass is claimed for cross-language handle equality. This testability disposition is not implementation validation, conformance evidence, or a waiver of the RTI obligation. Revisit direct coverage with an explicit mixed C++/Java federation fixture.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.11.3.3 requires the RTI to obtain an AuthorizerFactory implementation through AuthorizerFactoryFactory using the symbolic name HLAauthorizer. The official C++ API lets an application call the factory-factory and lets a TCK exercise authorization outcomes during Connect, but it exposes no portable observer for the exact internal factory lookup. The factory-contract scenario directly invokes the public factory API; Connect authorization scenarios observe policy decisions. Neither proves that the RTI selected its internal factory through this exact symbolic-name lookup rather than another path.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct portable C++ TCK mapping or pass is claimed for the RTI-internal selection requirement. The existing public factory and Connect cases remain evidence only for their separately mapped public behaviors. This is not implementation validation, conformance evidence, or a waiver of Umbra's §12.11.3.3 obligation. Revisit if a public-compatible factory-selection oracle is available.

requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct C++ TCK mapping or pass is claimed for this Java package/class/JAR requirement. This is C++-lane scope accounting only, not a waiver of the 2025 Java binding obligation or evidence of Java implementation behavior; a Java TCK lane must verify it.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.13.4.3 requires an RTI federate-protocol Resume Status message. The official C++ API does not expose this message type, its serialized bytes, or a transport-level receive oracle. Public federation-management calls cannot directly assert this protocol response; validating it requires a separate internal protocol or interoperability test, not a portable public-API TCK case.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct public C++ TCK mapping or test pass is claimed for this protocol-message requirement. This disposition does not establish the RTI's protocol behavior, implementation validation, conformance, or a waiver of Umbra's obligation; retain it for internal protocol-level verification.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §11.2.1 p. 288 l. 24 requires that the RTI not subscribe to any MOM object class. Public C++ Subscribe/Unsubscribe services declare subscriptions for an application federate; the API exposes no RTI-owned federate identity or portable query for RTI-internal subscriptions. The registry stores declaration state by joined federate identity and rejects nonmember identities, while RTI-owned MOM objects are tracked separately. A direct portable TCK trigger is not currently identifiable.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct public C++ TCK mapping or test pass is claimed for this requirement. Internal Catch2 case umbra-cpp-internal-rti-mom-subscription-member-scope checks only the private registry membership boundary; it does not prove the RTI's normative non-subscription behavior. This is not implementation validation, conformance evidence, or a waiver of Umbra's RTI obligation. Keep the requirement visible as not directly TCK-tested and revisit if a portable public observable becomes available.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.13.4.5 p. 403 l. 34 requires protocol sequence-number rollover from 0x7fffffff to zero. The official C++ API exposes no sequence-number state or raw protocol messages.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct public C++ TCK mapping or test pass is claimed for sequence-number rollover. The RTI obligation remains for internal protocol/codec verification; this is not wire-level validation or conformance.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.13.4.5 p. 403 l. 37 ties sequence-number uniqueness to bounded message-history buffers. The official C++ API exposes neither the protocol history buffer nor message sequence identities.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct public C++ TCK mapping or test pass is claimed for message-history/sequence-number uniqueness. The RTI obligation remains for internal protocol and interoperability verification; this is not implementation validation or conformance.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.13.3.3 p. 396 l. 147 requires Time Representation arguments in the federate protocol to use the HLA time type name. RTIambassador.Create Federation Execution accepts the public logical-time implementation name, but the official C++ API exposes no request bytes or protocol-inspection surface: a portable TCK can observe the selected factory, not the protocol argument's encoded form. Catch2 case umbra-process-federation-service-codec-time-representation-name-internal exercises the local process Create request codec for HLAinteger64Time and HLAfloat64Time; that is internal implementation evidence, not a portable TCK mapping.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct portable C++ TCK mapping or test pass is claimed for this requirement. The internal Catch2 test covers Umbra's private process codec only; it does not establish the external IEEE federate-protocol wire format, independent-provider interoperability, or conformance. Keep the requirement visible as not directly TCK-tested and revisit if a public wire-format oracle becomes available.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.13.3.3 p. 396 l. 159 requires handle arguments, except Conveyed Regions, to contain opaque bytes produced by the handle's encode operation. RTIambassador handle-taking services can trigger requests, and Handle.h exposes encode(), but the official C++ API exposes no raw federate-protocol request bytes or protocol inspection surface. The current getObjectClassName path converts ObjectClassHandle to an Umbra numeric ID and the private process codec serializes that ID; process_federation_service_protocol.hpp explicitly defines these payloads as private, already-decoded plumbing, not HLA wire encodings. Therefore this private representation is not evidence for or against the normative handle.encode() wire requirement.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct portable C++ TCK mapping or test pass is claimed; this remains 0% direct TCK coverage. Existing handle round-trip and private process-codec tests do not observe the normative federate-protocol argument bytes and must not be mapped as substitutes. This disposition is not implementation validation, conformance evidence, or a waiver of Umbra's RTI protocol obligation. Revisit direct TCK coverage if a public wire-format oracle becomes available; validate protocol encoding separately at the RTI protocol boundary.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.13.3.3 p. 396 l. 168 requires Conveyed Regions in federate service messages to be represented as a full ConveyedRegionSet encoding, not as handles. The official C++ API exposes regional services and callback designators but no ConveyedRegionSet type, federate-protocol bytes, or public protocol-inspection surface. Public regional routing can prove observable delivery behavior, but cannot distinguish full constituent-part encoding from private handle serialization.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct portable C++ TCK mapping or test pass is claimed. Existing regional-interaction-routing scenarios exercise public region routing and callback designators only; they do not prove the federate-service-message representation. This disposition is not implementation validation, conformance evidence, or a waiver of Umbra's RTI protocol obligation. Revisit if an independent-provider interoperability fixture or public wire-format oracle can inspect the conveyed region representation.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.13.4.4 p. 401 l. 58 requires the RTI to determine the Last Received Federate and Oldest Available RTI message sequence numbers while processing a Resume Request. The official C++ API exposes no public message-history recovery service or those protocol sequence values. The current adapter privately issues Resume Request and sees LRF in Resume Status, but Resume Status carries no separate numeric OAR; a public recovery outcome therefore cannot directly assert both required determinations. Private Catch2 process-transport tests remain internal implementation evidence, not portable TCK coverage.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct public C++ TCK mapping is claimed: p401-l58-19 remains 0% direct TCK coverage and is not a test pass, implementation validation, or conformance evidence. This does not waive Umbra's RTI implementation obligation; retain internal C++ tests for the history-bound decision. Revisit if the official API or a public observable recovery outcome exposes an oracle for both sequence values.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §5.1.1 p. 81 l. 104 requires every class to have at most one immediate superclass. The public C++ API has no class-graph construction or mutation service; Create Federation Execution consumes FOM module files. The pinned IEEE 1516.2-2025 FDD XSD represents object and interaction class inheritance as recursively nested objectClass/interactionClass elements, so each qualified class has one containing parent in a finite hierarchy. Repeating a simple class name below distinct qualified parents describes distinct classes, not one class with multiple immediate superclasses. A conforming public-API FOM therefore cannot provide the invalid graph needed for a direct rejection case.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct public C++ TCK mapping or test pass is claimed for p81-l104-31; this disposition records only the absence of a conforming public-API trigger. It is not implementation validation or a waiver of the 1516.1 RTI obligation. Keep the requirement visible as not directly TCK-tested, and revisit if the FDD model or public API gains a way to construct arbitrary class graphs.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §5.1.1 p. 81 l. 105 prohibits a class from being a superclass of one of its own superclasses. The public C++ API has no class-graph construction or mutation service; Create Federation Execution consumes FOM module files. The pinned IEEE 1516.2-2025 FDD XSD represents object and interaction class inheritance as finite recursive XML trees, with child classes nested under their immediate parent and no superclass-reference edge that could close a cycle. A conforming public-API FOM therefore cannot provide the cyclic graph needed for a direct rejection case.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct public C++ TCK mapping or test pass is claimed for p81-l104-31-cycle; this disposition records only the absence of a conforming public-API trigger. It is not implementation validation or a waiver of the 1516.1 RTI obligation. Keep the requirement visible as not directly TCK-tested, and revisit if the FDD model or public API gains a way to construct arbitrary class graphs.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: RL-404 documents p300-r002 as a detached continuation value from the SaveFailureReason Table 5 row. requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.13.4.4 p. 402 l. 20 requires Table 32 federate settings: FED_INT_HEART (60 s), FED_TIMEOUT_HEART (180 s), and FED_TIMEOUT_RECONNECT (600 s). The official C++ RtiConfiguration exposes an opaque additionalSettings string but does not standardize its contents or syntax, so a cross-provider TCK cannot portably set or confirm those values. Umbra parses all three in its process profile. Internal Catch2 verifies setting defaults/parsing and timeout effects, but those tests are not TCK evidence. Provider-specific C++ TCK scenarios exercise heartbeat timeout/recovery and reconnect expiry through the official C++ API, but this does not create a direct portable mapping for the grouped Table 32 requirement.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct portable C++ TCK mapping is claimed: p402-l20-6 remains 0% direct TCK coverage, not a test pass, implementation validation, or conformance evidence. The provider-specific scenarios cpp-tck.federate-reconnect-timeout, cpp-tck.federate-heartbeat-timeout-recovery, and cpp-tck.federate-idle-heartbeat-preserves-session are Umbra-only runtime evidence for behavior under local settings. They do not verify all three Table 32 settings or their standard defaults. Keep the grouped requirement unmapped because the standard C++ binding leaves additionalSettings syntax implementation-defined; promotion of a behavior-specific case does not validate that provider syntax.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.13.4.4 p. 401 l. 70 requires the RTI to decide whether all lost messages remain resendable by checking both the federate's history boundary (LRF versus OAF) and the RTI's history boundary (LRR versus OAR). The existing NextMessageRequest response-replay TCK observes one successful response retained and replayed after a connection fault; it does not exercise a non-resendable gap, isolate either history buffer, or distinguish the required two-boundary decision. requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §8.1.4 p. 181 l. 163 contrasts TSO ordering rules with RO messages, which are received in an arbitrary order. Inference: 'arbitrary' means the standard prescribes no particular RO permutation; it does not require the RTI to randomize or deliberately reorder messages. The public C++ API can generate RO traffic, but every single observed permutation is allowed. Requiring a later RO send to overtake an earlier one would add a rule not present in the standard, while checking that both callbacks eventually arrive cannot distinguish a provider-selected FIFO policy from an implementation that leaves the order unconstrained. The sibling timestamp-preservation requirement is separately covered and does not establish arbitrary-order behavior.
requirement_dispositions.evidence_boundary: No direct TCK mapping or coverage claim is made for the RO-order freedom. This is a testability/permissive-order disposition, not a test pass, implementation validation, or conformance evidence. It does not waive receipt of RO messages, preservation of an explicitly supplied timestamp, or the distinct mandatory ordering rules for TSO messages. Revisit if the pinned standard defines an observable consequence beyond allowing any RO order.

A finite set of observed values that happens to be continuous cannot establish a guarantee; requiring a gap or a changed order would add behavior the standard does not require. The point-range limitation is an application-use boundary, not a distinct RTI output oracle.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.13.4.6 p. 408 l. 41 restricts CTRL_NEW_SESSION_STATUS, CTRL_HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE, and CTRL_SESSION_TERMINATED to RTI origin. The existing provider-specific heartbeat-recovery TCK coordinates adapter-side suppression/resumption and checks later public service success; it does not observe these message types. Mapping such an outcome to the message-origin rule would be indirect; inspecting Umbra-private frames is not portable public-API TCK evidence.

A finite timing run cannot prove the absence of a guarantee across executions, platforms, loads, or conforming RTIs; asserting any particular delivery interval would invent a timing promise the standard does not specify. A portable black-box TCK therefore has no deterministic oracle for this negative guarantee.

requirement_dispositions.rationale: IEEE 1516.1-2025 §4.1.6 p. 49 l. 163-168 applies when a fault creates multiple independent segments, each capable of continuing as an HLA-compliant federation execution, and requires the RTI to select exactly one. Umbra's current process profile has one authoritative coordinator: runProcessFederationService constructs one EmbeddedFederationRegistry and one ProcessFederationServiceHost, which serves multiple client sessions against that same federation state. The public C++ API and current test adapter cannot create two independently service-capable RTI state segments; the standard leaves fault detection and mechanisms implementation-dependent.

The current single-authority topology prevents dual federation state; coordinator-wide catastrophic failure may leave no segment, which §4.1.6 explicitly allows. This disposition is an architecture/testability boundary, not implementation validation, conformance evidence, or a waiver. Revisit if Umbra adds replicated or partitionable RTI authority.

Direct bounded §4.1 p. 39 l. 4-1 witness: in one application process, four distinct public RTIambassador sessions remain joined simultaneously, with two federates in each of two independently named federation executions; all four joined-federate handles are valid. The primary scenario then exercises public object/interaction and time-management services in both executions. The contract runner reuses the same scenario body and is not independent logic. This proves the bounded same-process multi-federation participation path, not multiple federation joins on one RTIambassador, multi-process behavior, interoperability, or conformance.

Direct §4.5 p. 53 l. 43-7 witness: the public Create Federation Execution service successfully creates two differently named executions; List Federation Executions then reports both exact names in one report. This establishes the bounded create-and-add-to-supported-executions behavior exercised here, not every create precondition or provider-wide behavior.

Direct bounded public-API witness for no intercommunication between federation executions: a registered object, receive-order attribute update, and receive-order interaction are observed in the publisher's execution while peers in a second execution record no corresponding callbacks during a 500 ms window. A timestamped interaction at logical time 3 is then delivered in the source execution before its time-4 grant; an independently regulated/constrained peer in the second execution grants time 4 with no corresponding TSO interaction, including during a bounded post-grant observation. This covers only these exercised paths and does not establish isolation of every service family, every transport, or independent-provider interoperability.

Direct bounded §4.5 independence witness: two distinct federation executions simultaneously accept the same two exact federate names (including one ASCII case variant) through separate public RTIambassador sessions; List Federation Execution Members reports exactly those same two names within each execution. The existing positive controls and bounded receive-order/TSO isolation assertions also show selected behavior remains local to its execution. This is same-process coverage of the tested membership and delivery paths, not exhaustive independence across all services, transports, independent processes/providers, or conformance.

Direct bounded §12.8 witness: one connected creator RTIambassador calls Create Federation Execution twice, leaving the first execution live while creating the second, then calls List Federation Executions and receives both in one report. The calls are sequential; this proves one instance can create coexisting executions, not concurrent or parallel invocation of Create Federation Execution.

For §11.5.1, the scenario checks the SendInteraction PairList encoding (p.293 r.89, r.95; Table 5 p.299 r008), the initial Configuration.CallbackModel enumeration selected by the HLA_EVOKED/HLA_IMMEDIATE run (Table 5 p.295 r009), and the FederationAttributes record under RL-394 (p.297 r008-r013; p.298 r007-r008). HLAfederationName, HLARTIversion, HLAMIMDesignator, and HLAtimeImplementationName are asserted as JSON strings from the initial report (Table 5 p.302 r002). For §11.5.2 p.293 l.104, file-enabled SendInteraction appends its service record to the advertised text file and does not deliver HLAreportServiceInvocation to the subscribed observer. For p.293 l.113, two joined federates advertise distinct existing report files; each appends its own GetParameterHandle record, and the receiver's action leaves the publisher's file unchanged. For p.293 l.131, both switches are enabled for file-backed SendInteraction; this case appends exactly two matching records, one per call, after the initial file record, and parses the complete file as three adjacent brace-delimited objects with no separator under §11.5.2.1 p.294 l.17 and l.20. This remains one receive-order service path, not all service families. For §11.5.2.1 p.294 l.14, the type-40 Map value decoded from the public HLAreportServiceInvocation HLAsuppliedArguments is compared with the exact HLAargumentValue object encoded in the appended log record. This witnesses one structured value shape, not every Table 5 argument type. HLAargument fields follow RL-398 without relying on RL-399's disputed examples; GetParameterHandle HLAreturnedArgument follows RL-400, also avoiding RL-399's disputed examples. This does not claim complete Table 5 coverage or conformance.

It does not claim the p304-r001 continuation or disputed example literals. MessageRetractionReturn rows p298-r019/r020 are not attributed to Retract: the public C++ Retract API is void and this scenario checks its Null return in the separate void-return rule.

scenarios.title: Report one subscriber-specific discovered class per federate
scenarios.mapping_note: For Summary Rule 2 (§4), the publisher registers the object through the official API and all three joined federates resolve the federation-wide name back to their own local object-instance handle; subscribers also receive the instance through FederateAmbassador discovery and resolve its name and known class. This is bounded public evidence of the application-facing federate object-instance representation and stable federate-local lookup, not proof that the RTI holds no internal registry metadata or payload copies. Directly asserts that the same registered derived-class object is discovered exactly once by each of two federates, with the base subscriber reporting the base class and the derived subscriber reporting the derived class; Get Known Object Class Handle agrees with each subscriber's discovered class. This directly maps §5.8 p. 96 l. 75: each subscriber's callback identifies a class to which that federate subscribed, for these base-only and derived-only subscription shapes. For §6.1.1, the exact-class subscriber's discovered class equals the registered class (page-107-l39-9), the base subscriber's class is the closest subscribed superclass (l45-11), each callback carries that candidate class (l102-30), and discovery occurs for both subscriptions to attributes owned by the publisher (l51-13). The existing §5.1.2 mappings cover the discovery and known-class rules at page 083 lines 17, 68, 71, and 77. Each ambassador resolves its local object handle to the common object name; opaque handles are not compared across ambassadors. The adapter supplies the FOM hierarchy and names; setup and teardown are not separate normative claims.
scenarios.parity_scope_note: Java parity uses one publisher, one base-view subscriber, and one exact-derived subscriber. Each receives exactly one discovery with its own subscribed class, matching known-class result, and local handle-to-object-name resolution; the publisher retains the derived class and receives no discovery. Five current-source Umbra JNI runs passed under each callback model; other providers and conformance are unverified.

scenarios.title: Deliver two registered ordinary objects to two active subscribers and preserve identity
scenarios.mapping_note: For §5.1.5 p085-l173-56, the P0 FOM declares three TckObject attributes (Value, Name, PayRate); the scenario resolves all three handles for the publisher and both subscribers, requires three distinct handles per member, and publishes/subscribes that declared set. It then registers two distinct instances of the same class. The registering federate immediately resolves both known object classes as TckObject (p086-l6-1); both other joined federates receive exactly one discovery for each instance and report the discovered class as TckObject (p086-l12-3). For §6.8 p118-l34-7, each subscriber resolves the two registered instance names back to exactly the publisher's returned handles, witnessing uniformity for these objects across the federation. For p118-l37-8, discovery callbacks at both subscribers are keyed by the publisher-returned object handles, witnessing that same handle delivery to each discovering federate. For p118-l43-10 and its equality leaf, the cross-member name-to-handle assertions use the C++ API operator== to compare returned values; this directly witnesses that the API comparison operator governs whether the two handles are considered the same. Direct §6.9 mappings: each of two registered instances is delivered through Discover Object Instance exactly once to both joined subscribers; the two object handles are distinct within the execution; and both subscribers resolve both names to the same publisher-returned handles, witnessing uniformity across those joined federates. The additional direct mapping to §12.2 p353-l102-33 is witnessed by the callback recorder finding each publisher-returned handle at both subscribers, plus each subscriber resolving both instance names to those exact returned handles. This is a bounded P0 fixture witness; the public API has no class-attribute enumeration, so it does not claim exhaustive arbitrary-FDD enumeration or conformance. The separate §5.8 mapping remains limited to the count/presence assertions showing each of two registered objects is discovered exactly once by each of two active subscribers. Other callback and identity details remain supplemental.
scenarios.parity_scope_note: The Java peer uses the same P0 TckObject and three configured attributes through the official IEEE 1516.1-2025 Java API. It verifies two distinct registrations, exactly one discovery per object at each of two subscribers, matching producer/class metadata, subscriber-local name/handle/known-class lookups, and ObjectInstanceHandle.equals identity with the publisher-returned handles. Five focused current-source Umbra JNI runs passed under each callback model; the paired C++ scenario passed both models with valid focused evidence. Other providers and conformance are unverified.

scenarios.title: Reserve, consume, contend for, and reuse standard named object instances
scenarios.mapping_note: Direct §6.5 mappings: an empty set raises NameSetWasEmpty; a name beginning with HLA and a mixed set containing one such illegal name raise IllegalName; the valid member of the rejected mixed set remains available for reservation by another federate. A successful multiple-name request yields the exact requested set through the multiple-name success callback, with no single-name callback; a single-name reservation is separately checked to have no multiple-name success or failure callback. Direct §6.6 mappings: the owner registers a name only after successful reservation; while that reservation is held, another federate's same-name reservation fails; the single-name contention and success paths are checked not to use the multiple-name callback. Direct §6.7 mappings: a multiple-name release containing an unreserved name raises ObjectInstanceNameNotReserved and is atomic, as a different joined federate still receives failures for each name in the reserved set. After release, another joined federate successfully reserves a formerly held name, demonstrating availability after release. Direct §6.8 mappings: page-118-l58-15 requires the registering federate to own the supplied name reservation; a second published federate receives ObjectInstanceNameNotReserved before the owner successfully registers the same name. Page-118-l64-17 covers coadunation of that reserved name with the registered instance, checked through owner name/handle lookup and subscriber discovery. Direct §9.5 p. 229 l. 23-33 mappings: named registration with an unreserved name must raise ObjectInstanceNameNotReserved; after the successful reservation, registration uses that same name and verifies the name-to-handle association at the owner and discovering member. Two unnamed registrations produce distinct federation-wide instance names; the generated names are looked up against their handles and are discovered by the subscribing member without asserting a vendor-specific format. After successful named registration, owner release fails with ObjectInstanceNameNotReserved and another publisher's registration fails with ObjectInstanceNameInUse; these post-success consumption/in-use checks are supplemental. The owner also unpublishes the class, receives ObjectClassNotPublished on named registration, republishes, and successfully registers the same reserved name; this failed-publication reservation-retention check is supplemental. The reserved-name versus unnamed-registration collision check is likewise supplemental pending an exact pinned 2025 mapping. This is installed-package adapter evidence, not a provider-conformance claim.

Direct §6.7 evidence verifies that an invalid member aborts multiple-name release without releasing any held name, and that a released name can be reserved by another joined federate. The scenario also retains the direct §6.8 reservation-owner rejection and owner name/handle/discovery identity assertions. The post-success release/in-use exceptions, failed-publication/republication retry, and reserved-name versus unnamed-registration collision checks remain supplemental; no provider-conformance claim is inferred.

scenarios.title: Verify passive object subscriptions do not establish delivery interest or publisher advisory
scenarios.mapping_note: Direct bounded §3.1 p. 30 l. 22 and §5.8 p. 96 l. 144-45 witness for ordinary object-attribute subscriptions. The passive receiver subscribes alone: no Start Registration reaches the publisher, and after object registration/update neither the unsubscribed active receiver nor the passive receiver gets discovery or reflection. A separate active receiver then subscribes; the positive Start Registration advisory occurs, and a new object's update is discovered/reflected once at both active and passive receivers. This distinguishes passive interest from the active delivery-relevance trigger while verifying that the passive receiver remains eligible after active interest exists. Regional subscription variants and Stop Registration effects are not claimed. The direct installed-package run passed both HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE; results: out/mgw/cpp-tck-directed-subscription-current-20261104/passive-subscription-boundaries-20261104.json and .xml. scenarios.title: Remove the requested attribute from active and passive multi-attribute subscriptions across instances
scenarios.mapping_note: Direct bounded §5.9 p. 98 l. 11 and l. 32 witness: two already-discovered object instances each begin with both class-attribute subscriptions in scope. The active invoking federate's existing path unsubscribes Value, after which updates to each instance deliver only Name while Value-only updates are withheld; an unaffected active peer still receives both or the Value-only control. A supplemental passive subscriber also positively receives both attributes while active peers maintain delivery interest; after it unsubscribes Value, updates to both instances still deliver Name but not Value, and Value-only updates produce no passive reflection. Lack of reflection is the public observable that the corresponding instance attributes have gone out of scope; the API exposes no direct scope-state query. The p. 98 l. 17 -> §5.9 mapping separately covers the selective service result and preservation of peer subscriptions. A second supplemental state-isolation guard uses the adapter-supplied sibling-class fixture to prove the invoking federate's separate IndependentValue subscription continues to reflect before and after the base-class selective unsubscribe; these supplemental checks add no requirement mapping. Focused installed-package MinGW/Ninja CTest and direct JSON/JUnit pass under HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE; this is Umbra adapter evidence only, not independent-provider or conformance evidence.

scenarios.title: Remove all attributes from a class subscription with the whole-class service

The separate p. 98 l. 20 -> §5.9 mapping checks that a subsequent base-class update delivers neither subscribed attribute. A supplemental passive branch proves its public delivery boundary: a passive base-class subscription receives both values while a separate active subscriber maintains delivery interest; after the passive federate invokes whole-class unsubscribe, an active peer still discovers/reflects while the passive federate receives neither later base-object discovery nor attribute reflection. The two-module sibling-class fixture also proves that the same federate's IndependentValue discovery/reflection remain active after its base-class unsubscribe. These are bounded active/passive and sibling-state checks under the existing mappings, not additional requirement claims. The supplied-set branch is covered separately by cpp-tck.selective-attribute-unsubscription. Focused installed-package MinGW/Ninja CTest and direct JSON/JUnit pass under HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE (.build/cpp-tck-object-attribute-unsubscribe-sibling-20261114/whole-class-passive-unsubscribe-direct.json); this is Umbra adapter evidence only, not independent-provider or conformance evidence.

requirement_mappings.note: The requesting owner receives requestFederationRestoreSucceeded with the requested save label before FederationRestoreBegun and InitiateFederateRestore callbacks; the paired failure scenario covers a negative indication for an unavailable label.

For a valid Request Federation Restore, the test observes the ConfirmFederationRestorationRequest service report with the supplied label and true request-success indicator, alongside the public success callback.

Two joined federates invoke Request Federation Restore from a shared start gate; the test asserts exactly one receives requestFederationRestoreSucceeded. This is the bounded two-request case, not an arbitrary-N arbitration proof.
The competing two-member case asserts the other request receives requestFederationRestoreFailed, neither service call throws, and only one restore-begun/initiate callback set starts.
After a successful restore request, both joined members are explicitly asserted to receive exactly one FederationRestoreBegun callback before restore processing continues.

After both joined members receive FederationRestoreBegun, the test attempts a valid published receive-order Send Interaction. The official RestoreInProgress exception is required by §6.12 and the peer receives no application interaction, so no new information enters the federation during restore.

The successful two-member restore path gives each joined federate its FederationRestored callback after FederationRestoreBegun; the companion abort scenario checks that the terminal outcome is RESTORE_ABORTED when the restore does not complete.
Both joined members receive FederationRestoreBegun and both later receive FederationRestored on the successful restore path.

The test calls Send Interaction with valid published/subscribed handles after restore begins, observes RestoreInProgress, and confirms no Receive Interaction callback for the application interaction reaches the peer.

scenarios.mapping_note: The snapshot scenario invokes Query Federation Restore Status without a save-label argument while idle, during restore, and while one member awaits federation completion, and observes the response at the querying member. This directly covers §4.34's no-label query form and response requirement. Before any restore request, the query identifies both members by pre-restore handles; during restore, the response is matched to the post-restore designators delivered by Initiate Federate Restore. After one member reports restore complete while the other is still restoring, the query confirms FEDERATE_WAITING_FOR_FEDERATION_TO_RESTORE for the first and FEDERATE_RESTORING for the second. It also checks the response as a public HLAreportServiceInvocation during restore and, after restore completes, through the exact HLAreportServiceFile path advertised by Federate MOM. Its type-20 returned status set is compared with FederateRestoreStatusVector; the file assertion requires exactly two joined-handle records with NO_RESTORE_IN_PROGRESS. Runtime evidence covers three RestoreStatus values; the enum-contract case checks the six public enumerants are distinct. Existing p.297 r003-r006 mappings remain scoped to FederateRestoreStatus record fields; malformed collection row r007 remains unmapped. Public C++ development evidence only, not conformance.

scenarios.mapping_note: Clause 4.1.1 maps the direct Initiate Federate Save eligibility rule: both joined federates are unconstrained and receive their matching callback. scenarios.title: Verify collective constrained save admission and the non-constrained eligibility barrier
scenarios.mapping_note: The public C++ TCK requests an untimed save while two members are time constrained and neither is Time Advancing. A single TAR(5) does not start the save or initiate only one member; both constrained TARs are accepted first while save remains available. With both targets above initial GALT, the TCK observes one Initiate Federate Save callback for each joined member after both constrained TARs are accepted and before either constrained member receives a Time Advance Grant. Page-42 l10-3 maps to Clause 4.1.1's Initiate Federate Save eligibility rule: no callback while constrained members are idle, then callbacks once each is in the Time Advancing state and before TAG. The paired unconstrained-eligibility scenario covers the other branch of Clause 4.1.1. Other direct mappings cover untimed-save participation and member instructions under Clauses 4.1.2 and 4.19, plus constrained-member eligibility under Clause 4.20 and the pending-time-advance interval under Clause 8 at the broad normative scope recorded by RL-390. Clause 4.1.3 remains explanatory and is not separately mapped. The scenario does not issue a Time Advance Request during an active save, so Clause 8.8.3 is not claimed. Both callback models pass; this is local adapter evidence, not conformance or a claim about general time-management persistence.

Clauses 4.19.6 and 4.20 cover submission of a timed save at logical time 6 while the regulator is at 4 before FQR's actual grant at 5, and the constrained member's save-initiation callback at time 6 before the subsequent grant at 7. The distinct actual/optimistic grant assertions are supplemental here; this row does not claim a separate §8.12 requirement. No broader save/restore or time-management behavior is implied.

The scenario also advances initial time by epsilon, computes the resulting interval, and round-trips logical-time and interval encodings through the selected factory. Fixed encoding vectors now verify one positive HLAinteger64Time/HLAinteger64Interval value and binary64 1.0 for HLAfloat64Time/HLAfloat64Interval, and each joined federate's factory decodes those vectors. This is bounded direct encoding evidence for the selected standard types and values under IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.13.3.3; it does not exhaustively test all values or end-to-end timestamp transport. For §5.10 p. 99 l. 105, the passive receiver's lack of Turn Interactions On is paired with the active receiver's positive advisory control. Direct §5.1 receive-declaration witness: after the sender publishes, it sends one interaction before either joined receiver subscribes; the scenario pumps both receivers for the configured observation window and requires no callback. This covers the interaction-receipt component of p. 81 l. 35-9 jointly with cpp-tck.ddm-unsubscribe-preserves-other-class-subscription, which observes no object discovery/reflection before ordinary and regional attribute declarations and exact discovery/reflection afterward. This is bounded to the fixture's declared parameter sets. A base-class send containing the FDD-defined derived-only parameter throws InteractionParameterNotDefined without delivery (§5.1.4 page-085 l65). The valid derived send delivers exactly its supplied inherited/derived values to the exact-class subscriber (l74), projects only the inherited value to the superclass (l92), and gives each recipient one class view (l56). For §5.1.4, the callback parameter maps and byte values equal the supplied Receive Interaction arguments for both the exact-class and superclass projections (p085-l83-27); the superclass callback’s reported class is the superclass of the sent class, directly exercising promotion (p085-l107-35). scenarios.title: Exchange the 2025 New Session, heartbeat, and termination frames through the public API
scenarios.mapping_note: A byte-independent adapter peer constructs and checks Table 33/34 frames using literal standard bytes, not Umbra's internal codec. The portable C++ TCK invokes only the public RTIambassador API against that peer. Before any session exists, the peer requires the exact New Session request bytes, including Session ID zero (the value indicating no session exists), the invalid initial sequence value, message type, 28-byte packet size, and Table 35 protocol-version payload. It returns the literal Table 33 New Session Status bytes with a nonzero assigned ID. With FED_INT_HEART configured to 0.1 seconds through the public configuration path, the client sends zero-payload Table 34 CTRL_HEARTBEAT frames in the required federate-to-RTI direction; the independent peer observes the first within the bounded 550 ms tolerance and responds with Table 34 CTRL_HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE frames that match each heartbeat sequence. No HLA service message is exchanged, and every client heartbeat carries the invalid Last Received Message Number sentinel. The client Heartbeats and subsequent Close use valid, strictly increasing sequence numbers, excluding the New Session invalid-sequence exception. The peer verifies that Close uses the assigned Session ID and returns a matching Close Acknowledgement before the client transport closes. This is bounded direct evidence for p. 403 l. 31, l. 55, l. 70, and l. 76, and §12.13.4.5.3 p. 405 l. 16 (the federate sends CTRL_HEARTBEAT), plus the listed header, New Session direction/zero-ID, and established-session ID propagation clauses. It does not test sequence rollover, Last Received Message Number behavior after service messages or in mixed service/control traffic, RTI-originated heartbeat responses, RTI-side ID assignment, ordinary service payloads, every Table 33/Table 34 message, complete independent-provider federation interoperability, or full conformance.
scenarios.evidence_note: Fresh adapter-managed installed-package MinGW/Ninja verification on 2026-11-13 passed focused CTest 2/2 (HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE) and direct callback-model execution 2/2. Across four independent peer sessions, the literal New Session request used Session ID zero and the exact Table 35 payload; each session sent four zero-payload federate-to-RTI Table 34 Heartbeats with invalid Last Received Message Number values, received response-to-matching Heartbeat Responses, and used strictly increasing client sequence values [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]. First-heartbeat latency was 106–110 ms. Every Close used the assigned Session ID, received its acknowledgement before client EOF, and produced no protocol violations. Evidence: .build/cpp-tck-transport-public-new-session-java-port-20261113/results.json/.xml, Testing/Temporary/LastTest.log, and peer.json. The MinGW TCK image was 68,704,758 bytes with 0 DWARF; the focused tools/cpp_tck.py promotion check reports no findings. This is bounded evidence against the installed local provider, not independent-provider federation interoperability or complete conformance.
scenarios.parity_scope_note: The paired Java public-API case uses the same byte-independent loopback peer and checks Java connection configuration plus clean disconnect under both callback models. The peer observes the literal frames. This does not establish independent-provider federation interoperability or overall conformance.

scenarios.mapping_note: This adapter-required public C++ case creates two independent RTIambassador sessions, joins each as a distinct federate, completes List Federation Executions on both, resigns, and disconnects. A transparent loopback TCP proxy counts transport connections and inspects standard-defined headers. Direct §12.13.4.1 page-397-l114 evidence: two CTRL_NEW_SESSION requests carry the all-zero Session ID and each successful CTRL_NEW_SESSION_STATUS assigns a distinct nonzero opaque Session ID. Direct page-397-l117-38 evidence: the C++ assertions verify valid sequence numbers, strict per-connection/per-direction progression, the specified wrap, and the New Session exception. Direct §12.13.4.3 page-398-l87 evidence: the RTI returns the assigned Session ID through CTRL_NEW_SESSION_STATUS. Direct §12.13.4.5 page-403-l49 evidence: the C++ test requires the two successful RTI-originated CTRL_NEW_SESSION_STATUS frames to assign distinct nonzero Session IDs to sessions whose CTRL_NEW_SESSION requests carried the zero ID. Direct page-399-l53 evidence: each Disconnect sends one federate-to-RTI CTRL_CLOSE. Direct page-399-l62 evidence: the TCK observes a corresponding RTI CTRL_CLOSE_ACK on the same connection/session, checks that its Last Received Message Number equals the request sequence, and checks the federate-side EOF occurs afterward. Direct page-399-l59 evidence: after each public Disconnect completes, the adapter sends one valid Table 34 Resume Request using that terminated Session ID; the RTI closes the probe socket without returning a Resume Status, demonstrating that the old Session ID is no longer valid and the session was purged. This also directly exercises the RTI-side invalid-Session-ID socket closure in page-408-l86. Direct §12.13.4.5.4 page-405-l22 evidence: during the public Connect/service path, the federate emits CTRL_HEARTBEAT and the actual Umbra RTI process-service endpoint returns a CTRL_HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE whose response-to field matches the heartbeat sequence. Direct §12.13.4.5.5 page-405-l28 evidence: public Disconnect emits Table 34 type 5 (CTRL_TERMINATE_SESSION), observed as the federate-to-RTI close frame. Direct §12.13.4.5.6 page-406-l12 evidence: the actual RTI process service sends Table 34 type 6 (CTRL_SESSION_TERMINATED) on the same session and acknowledges the request sequence before client EOF. Direct §12.13.4.5.9/.5.10 evidence: public List Federation Executions invokes observed federate-to-RTI HLA_CALL_REQUEST and RTI-to-federate HLA_CALL_RESPONSE frames; the C++ test checks both directions and requires response Last Received Message Numbers to equal the requests on each connection. Direct §12.13.4.6 page-408-l65 evidence: each observed termination request receives exactly one corresponding response. Direct page-408-l74 evidence: the client closes its transport only after that response. Existing mappings also cover the page-408 service/callback direction rules and sequential service acknowledgement; pipelined requests are not covered. The case does not exercise HLA_CALLBACK_REQUEST/RESPONSE, so page-407 l. 9/15 are not mapped here. This is bounded to two sessions and one installed provider; no independent-provider interoperability or complete conformance is claimed.
scenarios.evidence_note: Fresh adapter-managed installed-package MinGW runs passed 2/2 on 2026-11-09 across HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE. The current-source process federation service fixture was rebuilt with MinGW/Ninja (11,325,509-byte image, 0 DWARF). For each callback model, two public C++ federate sessions completed against that actual RTI service. The loopback observer required federate Heartbeats to pair one-for-one with RTI-originated Heartbeat Responses by connection/session/response-to sequence; the C++ test also asserted the observed type-5 Terminate Session and type-6 Session Terminated directions and correlation, and both directions plus acknowledgement for HLA_CALL_REQUEST/HLA_CALL_RESPONSE service traffic. Both models passed all checks. Evidence: out/mgw/cpp-tck-clause-6_1-service-spine-mingw-20261107/tck-results/transport-message-directions-verified-20261109.json/.xml. This adapter-required scenario has no portable CTest entry (runner reports ctest=false); direct public-TCK execution and adapter assertions passed, and `tools/cpp_tck.py` reports no findings. This is bounded evidence for the tested provider, not independent-provider interoperability or complete conformance. Fresh direct evidence on 2026-11-13: the adapter-managed installed-package C++ consumer passed 2/2 across HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE; its result artifact is .build/cpp-tck-transport-session-cardinality-java-port-20261113/results.json, and the focused cpp_tck.py promotion check reported no findings.

scenarios.title: Reject invalid Session ID or sequence metadata during Connect

The portable C++ test requires ConnectionFailed for each attempt, and the adapter observes EOF from the client socket after each rejection. This is direct evidence for the federate-side receipt/abort behavior for these two New Session Status metadata cases only; it does not cover other message types, the RTI-host receiving role, independent-provider interoperability, or complete §12.13.4.6 conformance.

scenarios.title: Connect over TLS 1.3 with a trusted server certificate

The client trusts that certificate, whose IP subjectAltName matches 127.0.0.1; successful TLS connection proves that the server presents the trusted identity and possesses the corresponding private key. The official C++ API reports the supplied settings as applied, completes List Federation Executions, and disconnects. HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE passed against the installed MinGW package on 2026-11-08 (2/2); evidence: out/mgw/cpp-tck-clause-6_1-service-spine-mingw-20261107/tls-server-validation-20261108.json and .junit.xml. scenarios.title: Reject a duplicate negotiated divestiture while the original request is pending
scenarios.mapping_note: After a joined acquirer requests the published attribute, the current owner begins negotiated divestiture and repeats the service for the same object/attribute with a distinct tag. The second call must throw the standard AttributeAlreadyBeingDivested exception. While the original request remains pending, the current owner sends an attribute update that is reflected with its tag and producer identity, directly checking continued update responsibility. The test then verifies that the first confirmation request and its acquisition tag survive and that the original request completes only after Confirm Divestiture, covering the completed-request termination of §7.3 p. 156 l. 20. Public API behavior only; this is installed-package evidence, not independent-provider interoperability or overall conformance.
scenarios.parity_scope_note: The Java API mirror checks duplicate rejection, the current owner's continued update responsibility, preservation of the original confirmation request, and transfer on Confirm Divestiture with the adapter FOM in HLA_EVOKED/HLA_IMMEDIATE. Focused local-provider evidence only; no independent-provider or overall conformance claim.

scenarios.title: Complete a pending negotiated divestiture through Attribute Ownership Divestiture If Wanted
scenarios.mapping_note: The owner starts Negotiated Attribute Ownership Divestiture while the joined requester is eligible, then the requester asks to acquire the attribute. The owner receives Request Divestiture Confirmation and remains the owner while the request is pending. Instead of Confirm Divestiture or cancellation, the owner invokes Attribute Ownership Divestiture If Wanted; the service returns the exact divested set and the requester receives the acquisition callback with ownership transferred. This directly exercises one alternate-service termination path named by §7.3 p. 156 l. 20. It does not claim the separate Unpublish Object Class Attributes example is covered. Installed-package public-API evidence only, not independent-provider interoperability or overall conformance.
scenarios.parity_scope_note: The Java mirror checks the eligible-member assumption request, pending acquisition and owner confirmation, exact If Wanted return set, and ownership/acquisition callback completion under HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE. Focused local-provider evidence only; no independent-provider or overall conformance claim.
